statement: For any canonical ordinary CNF with m clauses, if the v0.5 minimum-incidence selected pivot has incidence d=m, then every live variable occurs in every clause; all clauses are full-width sign vectors; ordinary elimination of the selected pivot produces at most min(p,q)<=floor(m/2) distinct non-tautological resolvents and no retained clauses.
proof: Every live variable has incidence at most m because there are m clauses.
If the selected minimum incidence is d_min=m, then every live variable has incidence at least m and therefore exactly m; hence every live variable occurs in every clause.
Thus every canonical clause contains one signed literal for every live variable, so clauses are full-width sign vectors.
The selected pivot occurs in all clauses, hence there are no retained clauses.
For a positive-parent and negative-parent pair, removing the pivot leaves two full signed tails over all remaining live variables.
Their resolvent is non-tautological iff the two tails assign the same sign to every remaining variable, i.e. iff the tails are identical.

Canonical CNF contains no duplicate clauses, so for each tail there is at most one positive-pivot parent and at most one negative-pivot parent. Therefore compatible parent pairs form a matching and number at most min(p,q).
Hence m'<=min(p,q)<=floor(m/2). Canonicalization can only decrease clause count further.
